Q: How to compare datetime values versus date values using CodeIgniter's query builder A:

date('Y-m-d h:m:s') is not what you want; that expression means:

{4-digit Year}-{2-digit Month}-{2-digit Day} {12-hour Hour}-{2-digit Month}-{2-digit Second}

If a PHP date was needed at all, it should have been Y-m-d H:i:s.

return $this->db
    ->get_where(
        'jb_emp',
        [
            'employer_id' => $id,
            'status' => 'Active',
            'save_draft' => null,
            'DATE(create_date) <= DATE(start_date)' => null,
            'end_date >= CURRENT_DATE + 1' => null,
        ]
    )
    ->result_array();

  • 'save_draft' => null will render as `save_draft` IS NULL because there is no operator in the array key. The other null-valued elements will not render an IS NULL expression because they contain an operator.

  • For performance reasons try to avoid casting datetime values as dates during comparisons. Sometimes there is no way to avoid it, but just something to keep in mind. end_date doesn't need to be truncated from a datetime value to a date value, just compare it against the start of tomorrow's date.

  • Because your query only involves one database table, there is no need to qualify any columns with their table of origin.

Q: ImagePullBackOff error because of DNS resolve problem A:

The nslookup command shows that DNS Server is "10.41.128.98". but why pod log says like "lookup my.docker.proxy.com on [2001:100:100:11::a]:53: server misbehaving;"? It seems like DNS server is "[2001:100:100:11::a]".

A system can have multiple DNS servers configured – and it's very common to have the same DNS server via both IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.

When you have multiple DNS server addresses, usually programs will try them in some specific order. The error message looks like it came from a Golang program, and I don't know what Golang does exactly, but I believe it queries all the OS-configured servers until gets an answer – much like the DNS functions in the OS itself.

Nslookup differs in this regard, and always uses only the first server that was configured. So for example, if your OS has both 10.41.128.98 and 2001:100:100:11::a configured, then the OS will use both servers, but nslookup will always use the first one unless told otherwise.

And secondly, Why nslookup command shows "** server can't find my.docker.proxy.com: REFUSED", even though it already show 'my.docker.proxy.com' address is 10.251.186.33?

That's because nslookup actually makes two DNS queries – one for A records, one for AAAA records (IPv4 and IPv6 addresses respectively) – and the incompetently written DNS server at 10.41.128.98 returns an error code for the 2nd query instead of just returning an empty response.

A nameserver's authority is for the whole name, and cannot be specific to just individual record types – either the nameserver handles queries for the name for all types, or doesn't recognize it at all. The error code "REFUSED" should only be used when the nameserver doesn't handle that name at all.

Since the first query (for A records) succeeded, that means the nameserver is recognizing the name, and therefore queries for all other types must also succeed, even if the nameserver doesn't have those types, in which case the correct response would be a success reply with 0 records of that type. By returning a REFUSED, the nameserver is contradicting itself by saying that it recognizes the name and that it doesn't recognize it.

Q: Running node JS file directly is successful but through cron - failure - Error [ERR_REQUIRE_ESM] A:

I installed nodejs several years ago. I recently installed nvm and updated node to the newest version (25.7.0). This is where the issue is with the nodejs version discrepancy.

adrian@nfp:~$ nvm which current
/home/adrian/nfp-repo/login/.nvm/versions/node/v25.7.0/bin/node
adrian@nfp:~$ which node
/home/adrian/nfp-repo/login/.nvm/versions/node/v25.7.0/bin/node

I added the whole path for that version to cron and it worked as expected.

https://www.reddit.com/r/node/comments/2h5885/how_to_use_node_installed_with_nvm_to_set_up_a/ - This thread helped.

Q: Problem accesing global variables in main.c through .S assembler source file (MPLABxIDE) A:

Have you tried to:

; Definir variables manualmente en la RAM
extern      D3
extern      D2
extern      D1
extern      D0

instead?

Historically, C compilers used _ character in front of an identifier to avoid name clashes with assembler code, but today that's practically disappeared. Check if your compiler generates symbols with _ prepended, and change the assembler code correspondingly.

Q: Do compilers always round floating-point literals using roundTiesToEven? A:

Are there any compilers or compiler targets where rounding is not done using roundTiesToEven?

  1. If there isn't any today, it may change tomorrow. Best to code to spec, not to popularity. If spec is not reasonable to attain, add enough conditional code (asserts, etc. to detect the unusual compiler.)

  2. I don't know of any today. Yet why is unspecified uniformity sought? When code has a need for specific code to floating point result, consider using hex FP like notation 0x1.23p-45. It is less likely to suffer unexpected conversion.
